Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot

Build the Zava Order Desk triage agent live — declarative, grounded on files, no actions.

6 min·Microsoft 365 Copilot·Agent Builder
FilesAgentBuilder_OrderDesk_Brief.docxZava_Rush_Order_Context.docxZava_Order_Intake.xlsx
Prompt

Paste into the Agent Builder Instructions field

You are the Zava Order Desk Agent. You triage incoming rush orders for the Smart Launch Shirt launch.

When the user gives an order ID, look it up in the uploaded order intake file and the Zava context files. Then run exactly three checks:
1. Stock cover - can we fulfil the quantity by the requested date?
2. Margin floor - is the unit price at or above the 25.80 floor?
3. Compliance - region, contract terms, and launch-window rules.

Always answer in this structure:
- Order summary (customer, quantity, region, requested date)
- The three checks, each marked PASS or FLAG with one line of reasoning
- Recommendation: proceed, hold, or escalate - and name the escalation owner

Be concise and decision-ready. If a check fails, lead with the escalation. Never invent data that is not in the knowledge files.
Prompt

Test the agent you just built

Triage order ZO-3101.
Presenter

Build it live

Microsoft 365 Copilot > Agents > New agent > Skip to configure. Name = Zava Order Desk Agent; Description = triages Zava rush orders against stock, margin, and compliance; Instructions = paste the block above; Knowledge = upload AgentBuilder_OrderDesk_Brief.docx, Zava_Rush_Order_Context.docx, and Zava_Order_Intake.xlsx; Starter prompts = "Triage order ZO-3101" and "Which orders need escalation today?". Test in the Try it pane, then Create and share. Make the boundary explicit: Agent Builder consumes knowledge and answers - it cannot run actions or call APIs. That is why the end-to-end story in demo 11 (Copilot Studio for actions, then Agent 365 for governance) follows.

Sources: Agent Builder

Agent platform ladder (positioning)

Position Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, and Foundry on one ladder under the Agent 365 dome.

4 min·Positioning·Positioning
Presenter

Place each build tool on the ladder

This is positioning, not a live build. Make the relationship explicit so the audience stops seeing "random agents". There is one ladder with three build tools and one governance dome:
1. Agent Builder (declarative) - inside Microsoft 365 Copilot, fields + knowledge, no actions. You built this live in demo 7 (and demo 11, Door 1).
2. Copilot Studio (low-code) - production path with real tools, actions, approvals, MCP, channels, admin review. You build this live in demo 11, Door 2.
3. Azure AI Foundry (pro-code) - for AI engineers who need custom orchestration, evaluation, monitoring, and rollback. Not built live; position it as the engineering path.
Then the dome: whatever tool built the agent, it gets a Microsoft Entra Agent ID and shows up in Microsoft Agent 365, where IT observes, governs, and secures it (demo 11, Door 4). That is why we build first and govern second.

Presenter

Optional: Foundry pro-code framing

Only if the audience is technical. Describe a pro-code "Zava Fulfillment Sentinel" in Azure AI Foundry: ingest order events, retrieve policy and inventory context, evaluate risk, propose a recommendation, write an auditable decision record - with evaluation criteria, monitoring signals, and human-review/rollback rules. Stay verbal; do not try to build it live. The point is that Agent 365 governs even this pro-code agent.

Presenter

Presenter action

Use this as the executive platform close, not a feature dump. One sentence per stage: Agent Builder = fastest reusable agent (demo 7); Copilot Studio = low-code production with tools and admin review (demo 11, Door 2); Foundry = pro-code engineering path; Agent 365 = the control plane over all three (demo 11, Door 4). Do NOT mix in Visual Creator or other prebuilt agents here - they are a separate creative track and break the platform narrative.

Sources: Copilot Studio & Foundry

Microsoft Agent 365 end-to-end

The integrated arc: build it (Agent Builder), make it real (Copilot Studio), enable tools, govern the estate.

12 min·Copilot + E5·Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, Agent 365, Entra, Purview, Defender
FilesAgentBuilder_OrderDesk_Brief.docxZava_Order_Intake.xlsxCopilotStudio_Fulfillment_Agent_Spec.docxAgent365_Governance_Checklist.docxAgent365_Agent_Review_Register.xlsxAgent365_vs_PowerPlatform_Governance.xlsxAgentBuilder_Connector_MCP_Extension_Plan.xlsxZava_Public_OrderSignals_MCP_Registration.json

The integrated story. Demos 7-10 show each tool on its own; this runs the whole arc as one demo — four doors, one launch week.

Presenter

Door 0 — Set the compelling event

Frame the stakes before you build anything. It is launch week for Zava's NFC Smart Launch Shirt. Three rush orders are stuck in manual triage: Contoso Events (20,000 units, EMEA, critical), Fabrikam Sports (12,000, APAC), and Northwind Retail (8,500, North America) - 40,500 units, one shared deadline. One wrong commit blows the launch. The order desk needs an agent today; IT needs to govern it tomorrow. Then name the four doors out loud: 1) build it fast (Agent Builder), 2) make it production with actions (Copilot Studio), 3) enable knowledge and tools safely (connectors and MCP), 4) govern the whole estate (Agent 365).

Prompt

Door 1 — Build it fast: Agent Builder Instructions

You are the Zava Order Desk Agent. You triage incoming rush orders for the Smart Launch Shirt launch.

When the user gives an order ID, look it up in the uploaded order intake file and the Zava context files. Then run exactly three checks:
1. Stock cover - can we fulfil the quantity by the requested date?
2. Margin floor - is the unit price at or above the 25.80 floor?
3. Compliance - region, contract terms, and launch-window rules.

Always answer in this structure:
- Order summary (customer, quantity, region, requested date)
- The three checks, each marked PASS or FLAG with one line of reasoning
- Recommendation: proceed, hold, or escalate - and name the escalation owner

Be concise and decision-ready. If a check fails, lead with the escalation. Never invent data that is not in the knowledge files.
Presenter

Door 1 — Build it live (Agent Builder)

Microsoft 365 Copilot > Agents > New agent > Skip to configure. Name = Zava Order Desk Agent; Description = triages Zava rush orders against stock, margin, and compliance; Instructions = paste the block above; Knowledge = upload AgentBuilder_OrderDesk_Brief.docx, Zava_Rush_Order_Context.docx, and Zava_Order_Intake.xlsx; Starter prompts = "Triage order ZO-3101" and "Which orders need escalation today?". Test in the Try it pane, then Create and share. Say the boundary out loud: Agent Builder consumes knowledge and answers - it cannot run actions or call APIs. That is exactly why Door 2 exists.

Prompt

Door 1 — Test the agent you just built

Triage order ZO-3101.
Prompt

Door 2 — Make it production: Copilot Studio Instructions

You are the Zava Fulfillment Escalation Agent. You handle rush orders that the Order Desk Agent flagged for escalation during the Smart Launch Shirt launch.

For a given order:
1. Use the order-status lookup tool to get current fulfilment and inventory status.
2. If the order is at risk (late, below margin floor, or compliance flag), use the approval tool to request a human decision from the fulfilment lead.
3. Once you have a decision, use the Teams escalation tool to notify the fulfilment channel with the order ID, the risk, and the approved next action.

Always confirm back to the user: what you checked, who you escalated to, and the current status. Never commit stock or send an external message without an approval.
Presenter

Door 2 — Build it live with real actions (Copilot Studio)

Copilot Studio > Agents > Create > New agent (or Copy to Copilot Studio from the Agent Builder agent). Instructions = paste the block above; Knowledge = fulfillment spec plus order intake; Tools > Add a tool = add three actions: (1) Microsoft Teams - post message to the fulfilment channel, (2) Approvals - human-in-the-loop decision, (3) Model Context Protocol - read-only order-status lookup. Test in the built-in test panel until the escalation flow passes. Channels > Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Teams > turn on Make agent available in Microsoft 365 Copilot > Edit details > Save; then Save again to submit for admin review. The point: this agent can ACT - message a person, request approval, look up live status - which Agent Builder cannot. Presenter safety: in a shared tenant, show the tools configured and the "Save for review" hand-off; do not fire real Teams messages unless prepared.

Prompt

Door 2 — Test the full tool chain

Order ZO-3101 was flagged for escalation. Check its status, request approval from the fulfilment lead, and notify the fulfilment team with the recommended action.
Presenter

Door 3 — Enable knowledge safely: connector for Agent Builder (admin)

No prompt box here - this is an admin click-path. As MOD Administrator: Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Search & intelligence > Data sources. Show the Copilot connector pattern: connector deployed, schema registered, items indexed, admin consent granted. Then switch to Preston: Microsoft 365 Copilot > Agent Builder > New agent > Configure > Knowledge - show where an admin-enabled connector appears as a selectable knowledge source, and test with a Zava supplier/order-signal question. No live connector? Narrate the same pattern from the connector rows in AgentBuilder_Connector_MCP_Extension_Plan.xlsx - evidence, not a required input.

Presenter

Door 3 — Enable tools safely: MCP in Copilot Studio (admin)

No prompt box - admin click-path. Copilot Studio > Zava Fulfillment Escalation Agent > Tools > Add a tool > Model Context Protocol. Walk the non-secret registration: server name, streamable MCP endpoint, auth pattern, and read-only tools such as get_order_risk_signal and search_supplier_signals (reference: Zava_Public_OrderSignals_MCP_Registration.json). State the boundary: the same MCP server cannot be attached directly to Agent Builder - API/tool work belongs in Copilot Studio.

Presenter

Door 3 — Govern the tools (admin)

No prompt box - admin click-path. Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools. If Requests is visible, show the requested MCP/tool entry and the approve, reject, block, unblock controls. Walk the review questions out loud: who owns the tool, what data it can access, which agent can call it, what authentication it uses, whether tenant-wide consent is required, and what the rollback path is.

Presenter

Door 4 — Govern the estate: open the agent estate (admin)

No prompt box - Agent 365 is the control plane, an admin and governance surface. Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents. Find BOTH agents you just built: the Zava Order Desk Agent (Agent Builder) and the Zava Fulfillment Escalation Agent (Copilot Studio) - already listed, no manual registration. Open one to show its Microsoft Entra Agent ID, owner, publisher, and status. Say it: "I built these today and they already have their own identity that IT can govern."

Presenter

Door 4 — Identity: each agent is a real Entra principal (admin)

Microsoft Entra admin center > Agent IDs. Show object identity, owner, and the access package that defines what the agent can reach. Explain: Copilot Studio agents receive an Entra Agent ID automatically - that identity is what makes governance, audit, and Conditional Access possible, just like for an employee. Backup evidence: Agent365_Agent_Review_Register.xlsx (owner/platform columns show the same concept).

Presenter

Door 4 — Observe: one registry, one Agent Map (admin)

Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Overview - show the 30-day snapshot, total agents, usage trends, and actionable insights (pending requests, agents without owners). Open All agents for inventory, ownership, platform, and risk signals on both Zava agents. If available, open Agent Map to visualize which data and tools each agent touches.

Presenter

Door 4 — Govern: act on the agent lifecycle (admin)

Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Requests. Open the pending request for the Zava Fulfillment Escalation Agent (submitted from Copilot Studio in Door 2) and walk the Data and tools review: owner, data sources, tools/actions, target users, risk, mitigations - then publish or reject with a scope. Then show two more lifecycle actions: reassign an ownerless agent to a real owner, and tighten the Entra access package. Backup: Agent365_Governance_Checklist.docx. Do not click destructive actions live.

Presenter

Door 4 — Secure: Purview + Defender (admin)

In Microsoft Purview, point to DLP and audit coverage on the data the agent can access - for example, preventing it from sharing launch-contract data externally. In Microsoft Defender, show runtime protection that detects and blocks unsafe agent actions (unauthorized access, data exfiltration, prompt injection, tool misuse) and treats the agent as a first-class security principal. Portals not demo-ready? Narrate the control and use Agent365_Governance_Checklist.docx as policy evidence.

Prompt

Door 4 — Objection handling: Power Platform Governance vs Agent 365

Use data/agent-365/Agent365_vs_PowerPlatform_Governance.xlsx. The customer says: "We already have Power Platform Governance, so why do we need Agent 365?" Create a concrete answer using the Zava Fulfillment Escalation Agent and Zava Order Desk Agent. Show: what Power Platform Governance already covers, what it does not cover, what Agent 365 adds, and the exact demo click path that proves the difference.
Presenter

Door 4 — Executive close (say it, do not prompt it)

Close verbally from the controls on screen - do not ask Copilot to write it. Tie each control to the Smart Launch Shirt go-live: the Entra Agent ID gives accountability, the registry removes shadow agents, the lifecycle review stops a bad agent before it ships, Purview prevents a contract-data leak, and Defender blocks a compromised agent at runtime. Headline: "Launch week is no longer a risk. Every agent acting for Zava is identified, governed, and secured from one place - so Zava can scale agents with confidence." Known limits to respect: agent activity view is preview, read-only, user-scoped, 30-day retention; Defender/Purview agent surfaces depend on E5 and tenant configuration.

Sources: Agent 365 tools · Microsoft Agent 365 Frontier

Finance close: SAP actuals vs TM1 forecast

Move Finance from raw SAP/TM1 extracts to variance explanation, close controls, and CFO commentary.

6 min·Microsoft 365 Copilot·Analyst agent, Copilot in Excel
FilesSAP_TM1_Variance_Flat_Table.xlsxSAP_Actuals_May2026.xlsxTM1_Budget_Forecast_May2026.xlsx
Presenter

Open the finance close files

Open the ZAVA-Demo folder on the VM desktop. Use data/finance-close/SAP_TM1_Variance_Flat_Table.xlsx for the fast path, or upload SAP_Actuals_May2026.xlsx and TM1_Budget_Forecast_May2026.xlsx together for the heavier analyst path. Position the story as Zava's Finance team preparing month-end commentary for the COO.

Prompt

Find the biggest close variances

You are the Finance Business Partner for Zava's month-end close. Analyze SAP_TM1_Variance_Flat_Table.xlsx. Identify the top 10 absolute variances versus TM1 forecast, grouped by Revenue, Opex, Capex, and Working Capital. For each variance, show actual, forecast, variance amount, variance percent, whether it is favorable or unfavorable, likely driver, owner, and the follow-up action needed before close sign-off.
Prompt

Separate business variance from data quality issues

Review the SAP/TM1 variance data for items that look like timing issues, mapping problems, late postings, or manual journal anomalies. Create a close-control table with: issue type, evidence from the data, affected property or cost center, account, amount, risk to the close, owner, and recommended next step.
Prompt

Create the CFO close commentary

Create an executive-ready month-end close commentary for Zava's CFO. Structure it as: 1) headline result, 2) top favorable drivers, 3) top unfavorable drivers, 4) risks and open items, 5) decisions needed today, 6) wording for the COO update. Keep it concise, factual, and ready to paste into a close deck.
Presenter

Presenter action

Show this as the finance extension after the core Zava Excel section. The message is: Copilot can move Finance from raw SAP/TM1 extracts to variance explanation, close controls, and executive commentary. If Analyst is available, use it for multi-file reasoning. If not, use Copilot Chat with Excel upload or Excel Copilot with the flat table.

Sources: Analyst agent

Legal Agent in Word (Frontier): contract review

Summarize, risk-scan, playbook-compare, and redline a vendor agreement before signature.

7 min·Frontier / preview·Legal Agent in Word, Copilot in Word
FilesNorthwind_Property_Services_Agreement.docxContoso_Legal_Playbook_Service_Agreements.docxCounterparty_Position_Memo.docx
Presenter

Open the legal review files

Open data/legal-review/Northwind_Property_Services_Agreement.docx in Word. Keep Contoso_Legal_Playbook_Service_Agreements.docx and Counterparty_Position_Memo.docx ready for Copilot Chat upload or Legal Agent context. Position the story as Zava Legal Agent in Word reviewing a vendor agreement before signing a time-critical services contract.

Prompt

Summarize the contract for General Counsel

Summarize this property services agreement for Zava's General Counsel. Focus on commercial structure, high-risk clauses, negotiation pressure points, and what must be escalated before signature. Keep it to 10 bullets and cite the clause numbers you rely on.
Prompt

Perform a clause-level risk scan

Review the agreement for legal and commercial risk. Prioritize subcontracting, service credits, indexation, data protection, confidentiality, audit rights, liability, termination, governing law, and AI use. For each issue, explain the risk, cite the source clause, and suggest a negotiation position.
Prompt

Compare against the legal playbook

Compare the agreement against Contoso_Legal_Playbook_Service_Agreements.docx. Identify every clause that does not match Zava's preferred position or fallback. Create a table with: topic, current contract position, playbook position, risk level, suggested redline, and whether legal escalation is required.
Prompt

Draft targeted redlines

Draft negotiation-ready redlines for the highest-risk clauses. Preserve the original commercial intent where possible, but align with Zava's playbook. Focus on subcontractor approval, data processing purpose limitation, confidentiality survival, audit rights, liability cap carve-outs, termination fee, and AI tool controls.
Presenter

Presenter action

Use Legal Agent in Word if it is available in the tenant. If Legal Agent is not visible, use normal Copilot in Word for the open contract and Copilot Chat with all three legal files uploaded for the playbook comparison. Be explicit: this is legal operations acceleration and counsel review support, not final legal advice.

Feature matrix for this demo

Verified with Microsoft Learn. Scenario labels use visible product, feature, or agent names.

Copilot Chat and file upload

Can do: secure AI chat with web grounding, file upload, Copilot Pages, image generation, and agents. Limits: without a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license, Copilot Chat is not automatically grounded in Microsoft Graph data. Demo implication: upload or reference the Zava files explicitly.

Enterprise Data Protection

Can do: prompts and responses for Entra-signed-in users are covered by DPA and Product Terms. Limits: web queries and Anthropic-based capabilities have additional data-handling notes. Demo implication: position security clearly and avoid blanket compliance claims.

Excel Edit with Copilot

Can do: edit workbooks through chat, including tables, charts, PivotTables, and formulas. Limits: formerly Agent Mode; availability depends on license, client, rollout, and tenant configuration. Demo implication: keep the prepared workbook ready; use Chat with XLSX upload as backup.

Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents

Can do: create Office files directly from Copilot Chat and work with organizational data for licensed users. Requirements: Anthropic models must be enabled. Limits: region, tenant, government and sovereign cloud restrictions apply. Demo implication: treat as an optional wow moment; seed files are the backup.

Agent Builder

Can do: build declarative agents with natural language, add knowledge sources, test, and share. Limits: not on mobile; complex actions move to Copilot Studio; admin controls apply. Demo implication: build the Zava Order Desk as a declarative agent and do not promise external actions.

Agent Builder knowledge & connectors

Can do: add public websites, SharePoint/OneDrive content, uploaded files, Teams chat URLs, and admin-enabled connectors as knowledge. Limits: public URLs are capped; connectors require admin setup and are knowledge, not action tools. Demo implication: show public URL knowledge live and position the connector as the admin-enabled enterprise path.

Copilot Studio MCP & Agent 365 tools

Can do: add MCP servers as tools in Copilot Studio and govern BYO MCP through the Agent 365 Tools registry, requests, approve/reject, block/unblock, and observability. Limits: BYO MCP is preview; Agent Builder is not yet supported. Demo implication: MCP is the production tool path after Agent Builder.

Researcher and Analyst

Can do: first-party experiences for research and analysis in Copilot Chat Tools. Limits: availability varies by tenant and cloud; not in GCC, GCCH, or DoD. Demo implication: use as optional premium moments; keep uploaded-file Chat prompts as backup.

Teams Facilitator

Can do: collaborative real-time notes, AI Q&A, timeline markers, Teams Rooms support. Limits: requires Copilot + Teams licensing; some Planner/Word/Loop capabilities preview; not for 1:1, group, or external meetings. Demo implication: show live only when meeting policy is ready.

Teams Interpreter

Can do: real-time speech-to-speech translation in supported Teams meetings. Limits: requires Copilot + Teams + eligible base license; 20 hours/user/month; not for town halls, webinars, Teams free, Rooms-scheduled, or unscheduled 1:1 calls. Demo implication: optional global collaboration moment.

Microsoft Agent 365

Can do: observe, govern, and secure agents through a centralized control plane. Agent Builder, Copilot Studio, and Foundry agents integrate; Copilot Studio agents appear in the registry and emit telemetry automatically. Limits: some activity views are preview and tenant/user scoped. Demo implication: show registry, activity, ownership, risk, and governance actions after the build.

Sources: Agent Builder · Copilot Studio MCP · Agent 365 tools

← Back to catalogLicense & Frontier

What is GA, what is Frontier?

Use this before the demo to decide what to show live, what to position as optional, and what needs a backup path.

Copilot Chat baseline (GA)

Included with eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions: secure AI chat grounded in the web, Copilot Pages, file upload, image generation, previous chats, agents, and Edge contextual features. Not automatically grounded in all org data unless the user uploads/references content or uses an enabled agent.

Microsoft 365 Copilot license

Paid add-on: work and web chat, Microsoft Graph grounding, Copilot Search, the Copilot app, in-app Copilot experiences, built-in and custom agents, agent management, and advanced IT controls. The main licensing story for customer demos.

GA app experiences

Worldwide availability lists Copilot in Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, Loop, Clipchamp, Whiteboard, OneDrive, and SharePoint. Government cloud caveats vary by app; always check the row before promising GCC/GCCH/DoD.

Researcher and Analyst agents

Microsoft-installed first-party experiences for Copilot users. Researcher GA July 22, 2025. Caveat: built-in agents such as Researcher and Analyst are not available in GCC, GCCH, or DoD.

Frontier program

Opt-in preview channel for emerging Copilot and Agent 365 capabilities before GA. Requires Copilot or Agent 365 / E7 eligibility, admin enrollment, and user access assignment. Frontier agents appear with '(Frontier)' in the name and can take up to three hours to appear.

Frontier / preview examples

Agent 365 Frontier currently documents agents with their own identity and Shadow AI, AI provider model approval such as Anthropic, and AI-enabled Cloud PCs. Treat Legal Agent in Word and any 'Frontier' agent as preview/tenant-gated unless visible in the tenant on demo day.

Sources: Service Description — feature availability · Which Copilot is right for me? · Microsoft Agent 365 Frontier

← Back to catalogCustomer briefing

Why Zava works

Zava is neutral enough for any customer audience and concrete enough for a serious business demo: retail, supply chain, finance, sales, and executive decisioning in one storyline.

Microsoft Ignite uses Zava as a fictional athletic-wear demo company. This version turns that concept into a universal Microsoft 365 Copilot demo: one urgent order, scattered context, operational risk, margin pressure, and an executive commitment.

Feature grounding: Copilot Chat provides secure AI chat with Enterprise Data Protection, file upload, Copilot Pages, and agents. Microsoft 365 Copilot adds work grounding through Microsoft Graph, Office app integration, and broader agent access.

Sources: Microsoft Ignite BRK284 · Copilot Chat overview · Microsoft 365 Copilot overview

← Back to catalogLikely questions

Discussion answers

Copilot Chat vs. Microsoft 365 Copilot?

Copilot Chat is the secure entry point with web grounding, file upload, Pages, and agents. Microsoft 365 Copilot adds work grounding through Microsoft Graph and deep Office integration.

Why so many files?

Premium demos need real grounding: email, meeting notes, data, memo, risk register, Office artifacts, finance exports, and legal documents make the workflow realistic.

What is the main proof point?

The demo is not about prompting. It is a product-led decision flow across Chat, Analyst, Excel, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Agent Builder, Agent 365, Notebooks, Finance controls, and Legal Agent in Word.

What is the agent value?

The agent repeats the process for new orders and packages sources, rules, and escalation logic.
